name: Deliver a feature end-to-end
summary: The top-altitude journey of shipping a feature with Leafcutter: you say what you want and the acceptance criteria get authored (plan), the wired ticket is driven through its phase agents until it is green and committed (build), and the PR is merged and the epic/ticket closed (finalize). Each of the three stages drills down into its own pipeline flow — plan into define-a-feature, build into how-a-ticket-is-built, finalize into the finalize-feature pipeline — so this journey is the C4 L0 map over the whole delivery system.

steps.label: Plan
steps.human:
Say what you want; the ACs get authored.

I/O boundary: Plain-language input and reviewed AC YAML are the coarse journey boundary. JSON shows parsed AC fields; it is not a new planning service.

Contract fields and examples (generated)
Consumes:
  No checked JSON binding documented in this direction.
Produces:
  ac/id: string (required)
  ac/criteria: string (required)
  ac/readiness: string (optional)
  ac/assigned_agent: null|string (optional)
  Schema: [ac](config/ac_store_schema.json)

Output illustrative ac projection; not an execution receipt — ac; illustrative; selected fields only; full required/defaulted fields in linked contract:
{
  "id": "ACD-300",
  "criteria": "Given an approved requirement, When delivery finishes, Then its evidence is recorded.",
  "readiness": "draft",
  "assigned_agent": "python-coder"
}

steps.label: Build
steps.human:
The wired ticket is driven through its phase agents.

I/O boundary: The ticket remains Markdown. These are the real flattened driver planner and phase-response JSON contracts; completion is checked against ticket sign-offs, not inferred from an example ok.

Contract fields and examples (generated)
Consumes:
  SOURCE-REVIEWED DOCUMENTATION: Source-reviewed transcription of templates/workflows-js/build-ticket.js planner response schema (also used by build-feature.js); no new runtime registration or automatic JavaScript/schema parity.
  planner/ticket_path: string (required)
  planner/source_ac: array (optional)
  planner/ordered_phases: array (required)
  Schema: [planner](docs/product-truth/schemas/delivery-workflow-planner.schema.json)
Produces:
  SOURCE-REVIEWED DOCUMENTATION: Source-reviewed transcription of templates/workflows-js/build-ticket.js phase-result response schema (also used by build-feature.js); no new runtime registration or automatic JavaScript/schema parity.
  phase-result/status: string (required)
  phase-result/message: string (optional)
  Schema: [phase-result](docs/product-truth/schemas/delivery-workflow-phase-result.schema.json)

Input illustrative planner projection; not an execution receipt — planner; illustrative; selected fields only; full required/defaulted fields in linked contract:
{
  "ticket_path": "tickets/01_todo/feature.md",
  "source_ac": [
    "ACD-300"
  ],
  "ordered_phases": [
    {
      "agent": "test-writer",
      "status": "needed"
    },
    {
      "agent": "python-coder",
      "status": "needed"
    }
  ]
}

Output illustrative phase-result projection; not an execution receipt — phase-result; illustrative; selected fields only; full required/defaulted fields in linked contract:

  "status": "ok",
  "message": "The assigned phase completed; the ticket retains its evidence."
}

steps.label: Finalize
steps.human:
The PR is merged and the epic/ticket is closed.

I/O boundary: GitHub PR and Git merge operations are external artifacts. Parsed ticket readback and AC YAML progress are the structured records; this example performs no merge.

Contract fields and examples (generated)
Consumes:
  SOURCE-REVIEWED DOCUMENTATION: Source-reviewed transcription of templates/workflows-js/build-ticket.js readback response schema (also used by build-feature.js); no new runtime registration or automatic JavaScript/schema parity.
  readback/ticket_path: string (optional)
  readback/lifecycle_status: string (optional)
  readback/needed_phases: array (optional)
  readback/failed_phases: array (optional)
  readback/signoffs: array (optional)
  Schema: [readback](docs/product-truth/schemas/delivery-workflow-readback.schema.json)
Produces:
  ac/id: string (required)
  ac/work_status: null|string (optional)
  ac/implemented_by: array (optional; default [])
  ac/covered_by: array (optional; default [])
  Schema: [ac](config/ac_store_schema.json)

Input illustrative readback projection; not an execution receipt — readback; illustrative; selected fields only; full required/defaulted fields in linked contract:
{
  "ticket_path": "tickets/01_todo/feature.md",
  "lifecycle_status": "in_progress",
  "needed_phases": [
    "python-coder"
  ],
  "failed_phases": [],
  "signoffs": [
    {
      "agent": "test-writer",
      "status": "passed"
    }
  ]
}

Output illustrative ac projection; not an execution receipt — ac; illustrative; selected fields only; full required/defaulted fields in linked contract:
{
  "id": "ACD-300",
  "work_status": "done",
  "implemented_by": [
    "app/service.py"
  ],
  "covered_by": [
    "tests/test_service.py::test_contract"
  ]
}

acceptance_scenarios.given: a person with a feature idea
acceptance_scenarios.when: they describe it in plain language
acceptance_scenarios.then: the acceptance criteria are authored via the define-a-feature pipeline this step drills into

acceptance_scenarios.given: a wired ticket produced from approved ACs
acceptance_scenarios.then: the ticket is driven through the phase chain this step drills into until it is green and committed

acceptance_scenarios.given: a committed feature branch with an open PR
acceptance_scenarios.then: the PR is merged and the epic/ticket is closed via the finalize-feature pipeline this step drills into

provenance.note: L0 journey introducing the SUB-FLOW / drill-down hierarchy: plan -> define-a-feature, build -> how-acs-are-built, finalize -> finalize-feature.

Added source-bound field/type/requiredness/default metadata and explicitly illustrative JSON projections. Preserved topology, actor ownership, realization and AC status. Non-JSON artifacts and genuinely undefined proposed interfaces remain explicit.
